sentences.text: 2. Pursuant to the order dated 06.07.2023 the husband Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.5644 of 2023(5) dt.20-07-2023 and the wife and the I.O. of the case are personally present in the Court.

3. It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that without giving the benefit of Section 41 and in complete violation of the directions given by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar reported in (2014) 8 SCC 273, non-bailable warrant of arrest was issued against the petitioner and the I.O. of the Case (Rama Shankar Singh) accompanied with the O.P. No. 02 and her father went to Vadodara and got the petitioner arrested from the bank during office hours.

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar reported in (2014) 8 SCC 273
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. From perusal of the charge-sheet it appears that, though, the FIR was filed under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code but charge-sheet has been submitted under Section 420 and other Sections of the Indian Penal Code.
5. This Court fails to understand how the charge- sheet has been submitted under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code.

6. It seems that neither the I.O. of the case nor the D.S.P. concerned who was the I/c of the case and the then Superintendent of Police, City, Muzaffarpur has any knowledge of law.
Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.5644 of 2023(5) dt.20-07-2023 7.

The Magistrate who had issued the warrant of arrest has also acted in complete defiance of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar reported in (2014) 8 SCC 273.
8.

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar reported in (2014) 8 SCC 273
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant paragraph of the aforesaid judgment reads as follows:-
"Failure to comply with the directions aforesaid shall apart from rendering the police officers concerned liable for departmental action, they shall also be liable to be punished for contempt of Court to be instituted before High Court having territorial jurisdiction".
9.
In these circumstances, the I.O. of the case is directed to file his show cause as to why he shall not be punished for contempt of Court.

10. The then Judicial Magistrate who had issued non- bailable warrant of arrest is also directed to file his show cause as to why departmental proceedings be not initiated against him for violating the orders of the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
11. The show cause must be filed before the next date of hearing.

12. The then Superintendent of Police, City, Muzaffar (Niraj Kumar Singh) and the then S.D.P.O. /
Dy. S.P. (Ram Naresh Paswan) shall also file their show cause as to how they Patna High Court CR.

sentences.text: 13. Learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the O.P. No. 02 jointly submits that both the parties are willing to give one chance to their marriage and they will try to stay together.

14. In these circumstances, list this case on 17.08.2023.
15.
In the meantime, if the O.P. No. 02 wants, she may join her husband at his Muzaffarpur residence and thereafter the petitioner will take her to his place of posting as per his convenience.

16. Let a copy of this order be communicated to the Director General of Police, Bihar and to the District Judge, Muzaffarpur through FAX and e-Mail so that the Judicial Officer concerned and the Police Officials concerned file their show cause on time.
17.
Personal appearance of the I.O. of the case is dispensed with for the present.
